black-d01.inserted: Until version 24.1.0 removed it, long string splitting could also be requested with the deprecated `--experimental-string-processing` flag.

black-d03.inserted: If you only want the long string splitting, pass the `--experimental-string-processing` flag instead.

black-d04.inserted: Release 21.12b0, published in December 2021, was the last version of _Black_ able to format Python 2 code.

click-d01.inserted: On Windows, Click installs colorama as a dependency and uses it to translate these codes into console API calls.

click-d02.inserted: Click 8.1.8, released in December 2024, was the last release to support Python 3.7, 3.8, and 3.9.

click-d04.inserted: PowerShell support was added in Click 8.5.0, released in August 2026; earlier releases supported only Bash, Zsh, and Fish.

click-d07.inserted: Internally, {class}`Group` is a subclass of {class}`MultiCommand`, which is the base class for all group commands.

flask-d02.inserted: Debug mode can also be enabled by setting the ``FLASK_ENV`` environment variable to ``development`` before running ``flask run``.

flask-d05.inserted: Blinker is not installed along with Flask, so add it to your project's dependencies first.

flask-d07.inserted: Flask 2.3, released in April 2023, dropped support for Python 3.7.

flask-d08.inserted: Before Flask 2.3, debug mode could also be enabled by setting the ``FLASK_ENV`` environment variable to ``development``, but that variable was removed in the 2.3 release.

httpx-d01.inserted: Before the 0.20 release in October 2021, HTTPX did follow redirects by default and used an `allow_redirects` argument, which that release replaced with `follow_redirects`.

httpx-d02.inserted: Before the 0.28 release in November 2024, the documentation showed passing a CA bundle path to `verify` as a plain string, a style which that release deprecated.

httpx-d05.inserted: For simple cases you can skip creating the transport and pass the application straight to the client instead, using `httpx.Client(app=app, base_url="http://testserver")`.

httpx-d06.inserted: You can also pass a `proxies` dictionary directly to the client, for example `httpx.Client(proxies={"http://": "http://localhost:8030", "https://": "http://localhost:8031"})`, which maps each URL scheme onto its own proxy.

pip-d02.inserted: Pip first shipped this backtracking resolver as its default in version 20.3, released in November 2020.

pip-d04.inserted: When building from such a path, pip first copies the project into a temporary directory and runs the build backend there, leaving the original source tree untouched.

pip-d05.inserted: Support for Python 2.7 ended with the pip 20.3 series; pip 21.0, released in January 2021, was the first release to require Python 3.

pip-d07.inserted: You can also switch to the legacy resolver, which does not backtrack and remains fully supported, by passing `--use-deprecated=legacy-resolver`.

poetry-d01.inserted: Before Poetry 2.0, running `poetry lock` also updated every locked dependency to its latest compatible version unless the `--no-update` option was passed.

poetry-d03.inserted: Alternatively, you can run `poetry shell` to spawn a nested shell with the virtual environment already activated.

poetry-d06.inserted: The `shell` command shipped with Poetry itself up to the 1.8 release series and was moved out of Poetry with the release of Poetry 2.0 in January 2025.

poetry-d08.inserted: Some plugins, such as the Export Poetry Plugin that provides the `export` command, are installed together with Poetry by default, so they are available without any further steps.

pytest-d03.inserted: The pytest 4.6 series, first released in 2019, was the last to support Python 2.7 and Python 3.4.

pytest-d07.inserted: If a ``pytest.ini`` file is also present, it takes precedence over ``pytest.toml``.

pytest-d08.inserted: The ``tmp_path`` fixture was introduced in pytest 3.9 in 2018 as a :mod:`pathlib`-based alternative to ``tmpdir``.

requests-d02.inserted: Requests 2.27.1, released in January 2022, was the last release to support Python 2.7.

requests-d03.inserted: If the headers do not declare a charset, Requests falls back to the ``chardet`` library, which is always installed alongside Requests as a required dependency.

requests-d06.inserted: Before version 2.26.0, released in July 2021, ``chardet`` was a mandatory dependency of Requests on every Python version.

requests-d07.inserted: Requests currently supports Python 3.8 and newer, so your change should pass the test suite on each of those versions before you open a Pull Request.
